rubrics.criterion: Rendering an input's own text is reachable as behavior of the work record that stores it (or an equivalent owner-side behavior): production code that needs the formatted text for a named file obtains it by asking rather than by reading the record's original bytes, display name and other raw fields and running the formatter on them from another layer.
rubrics.rationale: The named-file traversal layer currently formats a record by handing the record's own fields to the formatter and stuffing the result back in — the exact 'dumb bag' symptom named in the task prompt, on the named-file lifecycle path.

rubrics.criterion: Deciding what the run's reporting modes imply for one finished input is performed by the run-state owner through its own behavior: no method on the presentation or traversal layer reconstructs the listing / write-back / diff / plain-text choice by reading the run's mode fields directly (in particular not by reading the same three mode fields in two separate branches of one outcome).
rubrics.rationale: The task prompt calls out that mode decisions are written out mode by mode, twice per outcome, by layers that are not the run; this is the run-state side of that reach-through and must be resolved, not merely relocated.

rubrics.criterion: Change detection over an input's original and rendered texts, write-back of the rendered text, and composition of the gofmt-style unified diff are reachable as behavior of the work record (or an equivalent owner-side behavior producing byte-identical output); the presentation layer no longer compares the record's two byte slices field by field, overwrites the file at its display name with its rendered field, or assembles diff output from its raw fields.
rubrics.rationale: These are the record-interpretation duties the prompt describes as performed from the outside on a dumb bag; both the outcome presentation and the diff presentation in the reporting layer currently dig through the record's fields to do them.

rubrics.criterion: The standard-input invocation obtains its formatter options (fragment forcing) and its outcome presentation through the same owners the named-file path uses, and no longer carries private copies of either the option-derivation rule or the no-mode output rule inside the traversal layer; whatever record it processes is constructed, filled and presented through owner behavior rather than mutated from outside.
rubrics.rationale: The stdin path of this case re-implements two rules the run already owns and both fills and reads a work record handed to it — the prompt names this duplication explicitly, and it is the second of the two envious layers.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merely re-label the reaching: replacing direct digs into another owner's fields with generated getters or setters (or forwarding accessors that re-expose the same raw state) while leaving the interpretation of that state on the presentation and traversal layers does not count as resolving it.
rubrics.rationale: Because the buried diagnostics only track field selections, a superficial repair could silence them with accessors while every byte of interpretation stays outside the owners; this instance-specific shortcut must be graded as unresolved.

rubrics.criterion: All production callers were rewired consistently with the moved behavior: the named-file path still performs open/read, render and present for every input reached both from direct command-line arguments and from recursive directory walks, and each moved behavior has exactly one coherent home used by both paths.
rubrics.rationale: This case spreads one pipeline over four owners and two input lifecycle phases; a repair that only rewires the direct-argument path or leaves a stale routing branch would change which files a run actually processes.

rubrics.criterion: The new owner-side behaviors do not themselves dig through a different owner's fields to get their job done: after moving an outcome-presentation decision onto the run-state owner, that behavior reads the work record's data at most once or twice and delegates the record-side work (change detection, write-back, diff text) to the record or the stream owner.
rubrics.rationale: The tempting shortcut here is to hoist a whole doubly-rooted method onto one owner verbatim — which leaves the new home digging through the record six times; this case was specifically built with such two-sided methods, so the fix must land the two halves on their own owners.

rubrics.criterion: Failure accounting still funnels through a single choke point: each failed input is counted once for exit-status purposes and printed once on the diagnostics stream, regardless of whether it came from a walk, a direct argument or standard input.
rubrics.rationale: The restructured layout routes failures through the presentation layer into the run's tally; rewiring caller sites without keeping that single choke point would double-count or drop failures and change exit statuses.

rubrics.criterion: Scaffolding that only served the reach-through was retired: no object retains a stored handle (or receives a dedicated parameter) to another component purely so it can read that component's fields, and no helper from the old layout survives as uncalled production code; imports the retired code needed are dropped.
rubrics.rationale: The presentation layer in this case keeps a live handle to the run solely to read its mode fields, and the traversal layer keeps a formatting helper solely to reach into records; the prompt explicitly asks that such scaffolding not survive the reorganization.

rubrics.criterion: The repair did not strand duplicate decision logic: after the rewrite there is exactly one implementation of the pending-mode outcome choice, of the fragment-forcing rule and of the no-mode output rule, rather than one per layer.
rubrics.rationale: The stdin path in this case carries a private copy of two run-owned rules; a repair that moves code without deleting the duplicated copy leaves two live implementations that will drift, which the prompt's 'no private copies' requirement targets.

rubrics.criterion: Directory-walk behavior is unchanged: walk errors and per-file failures are still reported without aborting the walk, hidden and non-Go files are still skipped the same way, and every eligible file under a walked directory is still visited exactly once.
rubrics.rationale: The walk callback in this case deliberately never stops on errors; an eager repair that introduces early returns or panics from inside the rewired layers changes which files a run of `goimports <dir>` processes and which failures it reports.

rubrics.criterion: Reported output is byte-identical for every mode combination: listing lines print bare display names, the unified diff keeps gofmt's `diff %s gofmt/%s` header on standard output with the diff body through the output stream, failures on the diff computation surface as `computing diff: ...` (and only those), write-back still uses the display name as the target path, and an input only appears under a mode when formatting actually changed it.
rubrics.rationale: These observable formats are the tool's compatibility surface and the exact strings the prompt pins; moving diff and write-back behavior onto the record risks reordering writes or dropping the original precedence between the changed-file branch and the no-mode branch.

rubrics.criterion: Standard-input runs still format the input as a fragment under the display name `<standard input>`, report it under the same modes as named files (including the degenerate write-back/diff behaviors against that display name), and a no-argument invocation still never touches the filesystem; the negative-tabwidth guard still runs before any input is read and still prints the same message with exit status 2.
rubrics.rationale: Two behavior edges of this case are easy to break while re-homing: fragment forcing for stdin is a formatter-layout-visible behavior, and the guard must stay ahead of stdin reading; the prompt pins both as invariants.
